sources.citation: Bennett, Ryan. 2016. Mayan phonology. Language and Linguistics Compass 10: 469-514.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions Chicomuceltec only as Huastec's extinct sibling (s > θ shift, citing Norcliffe 2003); no stress information for Chicomuceltec.

sources.citation: Kondic, Snjezana. 2012. A Grammar of South Eastern Huastec (PhD thesis); Herrera Zendejas 2014 Mapa fónico de las lenguas mexicanas; Meléndez 2017 (Huasteco de Mamey thesis)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Chicomuceltec discussed only for classification/history (Kondic §1.3; HZ pp. on Huastecan); no statement about Chicomuceltec stress.

sources.citation: Campbell, Lyle. 1988. The Linguistics of Southeast Chiapas, Mexico (Papers of the New World Archaeological Foundation 50). Provo: NWAF/BYU. Ch. 5 'Chicomuceltec', pp. 199-212; References pp. 404-418.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing explicit. p.202: 'The total Chicomuceltec corpus is about 500 lexical items.. recorded with no great phonetic accuracy'; defers Huastecan historical phonology to Kaufman 1980. Cited forms from Sapper (S), Termer (T) and the 1970s rememberers carry acute accents, virtually always on the final syllable (p.200: tahbál, kunín / S cuním / T kuním, S ajtíc, tokó / T tokó, to?ól, S osóu / T osóu, S,T vitím, seywé, metát, pičí, S,T chenúk, ač'ám) -- transcription practice only, no rule stated.

sources.citation: Termer, Franz. 1930. Über die Mayasprache von Chicomucelo. Proceedings of the 23rd International Congress of Americanists (New York 1928), pp. 926-936.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement. Only orthographic remark (p.927): 'In der Orthographie ist die spanische Schreibweise gewählt worden, um eine Vergleichung mit den älteren Aufzeichnungen zu erleichtern.' 284-word vocabulary (with Sapper's list and Stoll's Huaxteca) uses acute accents, not discussed.

sources.citation: Sapper, Karl. 1897. Das nördliche Mittel-Amerika nebst einem Ausflug nach dem Hochland von Anahuac. Braunschweig: Vieweg (Chicomucelteca pp. 243, 392-395; comparative vocabulary Beilage 4, pp. 407-436).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Chicomucelteca stress; the only accent remark in the book (p.288) concerns the Kekchi prayer texts. Word list only.

sources.citation: Campbell, Lyle & Una Canger. 1978. Chicomuceltec's last throes. International Journal of American Linguistics 44(3): 228-230.

sources.note: Primary report of the last rememberers' forms with phonetic transcription (accented); may comment on stress of elicited forms.

sources.citation: Norcliffe, Elisabeth. 2003. The Reconstruction of Proto-Huastecan. MA thesis, University of Canterbury, viii+215 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Reconstructs Proto-Huastecan phonology from Huastec + Chicomuceltec; likely evaluates the accent marks in the Chicomuceltec sources against Huastec weight-sensitive stress and may state a Chicomuceltec/Proto-Huastecan stress rule.

sources.citation: Kaufman, Terrence. 1980. Pre-Columbian borrowings involving Huastec. In K. Klar et al. (eds.), American Indian and Indo-European Studies in Honor of Madison S. Beeler, 101-112. The Hague: Mouton. (and Kaufman 1985, Aspects of Huastec dialectology and historical phonology, IJAL 51: 473-476)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Campbell 1988 calls it the most extensive treatment of Huastecan historical phonology; may characterise Proto-Huastecan/Chicomuceltec accent.

sources.citation: Zimmermann, Günter. 1955. Das Cotoque: die Maya-Sprache von Chicomucelo. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 80(1): 59-87. (Spanish tr.: El cotoque, la lengua mayense de Chicomucelo. Traducciones mesoamericanistas 1: 27-72. México: SMA, 1966.)

sources.note: The only philological analysis of the entire ~500-item corpus (Sapper, Termer, 1775 confesionario); if any author commented on Betonung/accent placement it is Zimmermann. Named by the earlier scan as the source.
